statement: A pi package is the harness's unit for sharing extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes through npm or git.
quote: Pi packages bundle extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes so you can share them through npm or git.

statement: A pi package declares its resources in package.json under the `pi` key, or relies on conventional directories.
quote: A package can declare resources in `package.json` under the `pi` key, or use conventional directories.

statement: Pi accepts three package source types: npm, git and local paths.
quote: Pi accepts three source types in settings and `pi install`.

statement: npm-style pi packages pin versions in the spec, and pinned specs are skipped by package updates.
quote: Versioned specs are pinned and skipped by package updates (`pi update --extensions`, `pi update --all`).

statement: Pi installs npm packages into a per-scope directory: ~/.pi/agent/npm/ for user installs, .pi/npm/ for project installs.
quote:
User installs go under `~/.pi/agent/npm/`.
- Project installs go under `.pi/npm/`.

statement: git-source pi packages are pinned to a tag or commit, and pi's update commands reconcile the clone to that pinned ref rather than moving it.
quote: Refs are pinned tags or commits. `pi update --extensions` and `pi update --all` do not move them to newer refs, but they do reconcile an existing clone to the configured ref.

statement: Moving a git-source pi package to a newer version is an explicit reinstall naming the new ref.
quote: Use `pi install git:host/user/repo@new-ref` to update settings and move an existing package to a new pinned ref.

statement: git-source pi packages are cloned under ~/.pi/agent/git/<host>/<path> globally, or .pi/git/<host>/<path> for project installs.
quote: Cloned to `~/.pi/agent/git/<host>/<path>` (global) or `.pi/git/<host>/<path>` (project).

statement: When a git-source package's checkout changes, pi resets and cleans the clone and runs npm install if the package has a package.json.
quote: When reconciliation changes the checkout, pi resets and cleans the clone, then runs `npm install` if `package.json` exists.

statement: pi install defaults to user settings; -l writes the package declaration to project settings .pi/settings.json.
quote: By default, `install` and `remove` write to user settings (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`). Use `-l` to write to project settings (`.pi/settings.json`) instead.

statement: Project settings can be committed for a team, and pi installs any missing declared packages automatically on startup after the project is trusted.
quote: Project settings can be shared with your team, and pi installs any missing packages automatically on startup after the project is trusted.

statement: A local-path pi package is added to settings without copying it.
quote: Local paths point to files or directories on disk and are added to settings without copying.

statement: When pi installs a package from npm or git it runs npm install, so the package's declared dependencies are installed with it.
quote: When pi installs a package from npm or git, it runs `npm install`, so those dependencies are installed automatically.

statement: Packages tagged `pi-package` are listed in the package gallery at pi.dev/packages.
quote: The [package gallery](https://pi.dev/packages) displays packages tagged with `pi-package`.

statement: Pi warns that packages run with full system access: extensions execute arbitrary code and skills can instruct the model to run executables.
quote: Pi packages run with full system access. Extensions execute arbitrary code, and skills can instruct the model to perform any action including running executables. Review source code before installing third-party packages.

statement: Pi loads skills from global locations including ~/.agents/skills/, and from project locations including .agents/skills/ in the cwd and ancestor directories up to the git repo root.
quote:
Pi loads skills from:

- Global:
  - `~/.pi/agent/skills/`
  - `~/.agents/skills/`
- Project (only after the project is trusted):
  - `.pi/skills/`
  - `.agents/skills/` in `cwd` and ancestor directories (up to git repo root, or filesystem root when not in a repo)

statement: A pi package can contribute skills through a skills/ directory or a pi.skills entry in package.json.
quote: Packages: `skills/` directories or `pi.skills` entries in `package.json`

statement: When two skill locations declare the same name, pi warns and keeps the first skill found.
quote: Name collisions (same name from different locations) warn and keep the first skill found.

statement: A skill is a directory whose only required file is SKILL.md; everything else in the folder is freeform.
quote: A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file. Everything else is freeform.

statement: Pi implements the Agent Skills standard, warning about violations but remaining lenient.
quote: Pi implements the [Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.io/specification), warning about most violations but remaining lenient.

statement: Pi extensions are TypeScript modules that can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, and add commands.
quote: Extensions are TypeScript modules that extend pi's behavior. They can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, add commands, and more.

statement: Pi extensions run with the user's full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code.
quote: Extensions run with your full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code. Only install from sources you trust.

statement: Extensions are shared through npm or git as pi packages.
quote: To share extensions via npm or git as pi packages, see [packages.md](packages.md).

statement: pi packages can also contribute prompt templates through a prompts/ directory or pi.prompts entries in package.json.
quote: Packages: `prompts/` directories or `pi.prompts` entries in `package.json`

statement: The settings key `packages` is an array of npm/git packages to load resources from.
quote: | `packages` | array | `[]` | npm/git packages to load resources from |

statement: Pi can enable or disable resources from installed packages and local directories through the pi config command.
quote: Use `pi config` to enable or disable extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes from installed packages and local directories.
